rules: An automation is a graph of blocks. Each block is { id, type, options }.
Use short local ids such as t1, a1, c1. They are replaced by real ids when the automation is saved.
Exactly one block has type trigger. It holds options.triggers: [{ name, options }] and points to the first step with nextBlockId.

Block types action, condition, chat, ai, api and field-operation are containers: they hold a list of plugins under actions, conditions, messages, ais, apis or fieldOperations. Each plugin is { name, options } and runs in order.
A delay block holds a single plugin under options.delay: { name, options }.
javascript and randomizer blocks have no plugins; their options are described by flow_block_details.

Blocks connect only through fields ending in NextBlockId (nextBlockId, errorNextBlockId, trueNextBlockId, falseNextBlockId, button and branch nextBlockId). Every value must be the id of another block in the same automation. An empty or missing nextBlockId ends the session.

Plugin names must come from flow_block_catalog. Call flow_block_details for a plugin before configuring it, unless it comes unchanged from a recipe; its inputParameters/outputParameters show which session values it reads and writes.
IDs inside options (stages, tags, instances, attendants, additional fields, pipelines) must be real ids of this workspace, looked up with the matching list tools. Never invent them.
Text options accept session values with {parameterName}, e.g. {leadFirstName}. Additional fields use {additional-field[<name>]}.
Automations are always saved inactive. The user reviews and activates them in the automation editor.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the automation starts.
Block that runs after every action succeeds.
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when an action fails. Without it the session stops on error.

connections.trueNextBlockId: Block that runs when the conditions pass.
connections.falseNextBlockId: Block that runs when the conditions fail.
connections.conditions[].nextBlockId: Optional per-condition shortcut: when that condition passes, jump straight to this block.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the messages are sent (or after the awaited reply arrives).
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when sending fails.
connections.messages[].options.buttons[].nextBlockId: Block that runs when the contact clicks that button.

options.instanceId: Messaging instance to send from (instance_list). Leave instanceId, platform and provider empty to use the lead's current contact instance.
options.platform: Platform of the chosen instance, e.g. WHATSAPP. Required together with instanceId.
options.provider: Provider of the chosen instance, e.g. z-api. Required together with instanceId.
options.contactId: Fixed contact to send to. Leave empty to send to the lead in the session.
options.isAnnotation: true to register the messages as internal notes instead of sending them.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the wait.

options.refreshLeadDataOnResume: true to reload lead data when the wait ends.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the AI steps.
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when an AI step fails.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the requests succeed.
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when a request fails.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the operations.
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when an operation fails.

connections.nextBlockId: Block that runs after the script.
connections.errorNextBlockId: Block that runs when the script throws or times out.

options.javascriptCode: Code to run. Has session.getValue, session.setValue and session.datasources. Its return value is saved to the datasource.
options.timeout: Seconds before the script is aborted (1-300, default 30).
options.datasourceName: Name the returned value is saved under.

connections.randomizers[].nextBlockId: Block that runs for that branch.

options.randomizers: Branches: [{ name, perc, nextBlockId }]. Percentages should add up to 100.

recipes.title: Thank the customer and move a won business
recipes.whenToUse: After a business is won: send a thank-you message to the contact and move the business to a post-sale stage.

placeholders.<POST_SALE_STAGE_ID>: Stage the won business moves to (pipeline_stage_list).

options.text: Obrigado pela confiança, {leadFirstName}! Em breve nossa equipe entra em contato com os próximos passos.

recipes.title: Tag the lead when a message mentions a keyword
recipes.whenToUse: When a contact writes about a subject, such as a quote or a price, mark the lead with a tag so the team can find it.

recipes.title: Distribute new leads among attendants
recipes.whenToUse: Give every new lead an owner, rotating between attendants.

recipes.title: Answer messages that arrive outside business hours
recipes.whenToUse: Tell contacts who write outside business hours when the team will answer.

options.text: Recebemos sua mensagem! Atendemos de segunda a sexta, das 9h às 18h, e retornamos assim que possível.

recipes.title: Remind the contact when a business stays in a stage
recipes.whenToUse: Follow up with the contact when a business is still in the same stage a few days after entering it, such as an unanswered proposal.

placeholders.<STAGE_ID>: Stage to watch (pipeline_stage_list), used both to start and to check.

options.text: Oi, {leadFirstName}! Ficou alguma dúvida sobre a proposta? Estou à disposição.

recipes.title: Ask a question and follow up when there is no answer
recipes.whenToUse: Ask the contact something and send one reminder if they do not answer within a day.

options.text: Oi, {leadFirstName}! Posso te ajudar a finalizar a sua compra?
Só passando para lembrar: estou por aqui se precisar de ajuda!
